brief: A herb planter of three cells side by side, each with a bin that drains.

requirements.evidence: Three full bases at q=-1,0,0 / 0,0,0 / 1,0,0 in a straight row (piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) locked with joint bolts.

requirements.requirement: Each cell has a bin that drains
requirements.evidence: Bin, full depth, drained (hex-bin-full-drain) in each cell: bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain – each has drainage holes in base.
All three drained bins filled to rim with soil and planted with herb plug plants (basil-young, mint-young, parsley-young) – visible in look view, meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Built a linear 3-cell planter: three adjacent hex bases side-by-side, each fitted with a full-depth drained bin, joints locked and open faces capped. Each bin filled with soil and planted with a different young herb for demonstration – ready for herbs.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: A three-in-a-row planter with drainage — I'll start your build.
